messages:
Lee (customer-success): Heads-up — Ravenwood is seeing p99 tail jumps on their Dedicated pool (us-west-2) since ~2026-03-16T14:05Z. Baseline p99 ~310ms, now spiking to ~2.3s intermittently. They reported it correlates with heavy embedding jobs. Can we triage?
Maria (support): Thanks Lee. Do we have request ids / sample timestamps from customer? I asked them and they sent three sample request ids. Pasting below.
Lee (customer-success): request ids: r_20260316_141207_1, r_20260316_141320_2, r_20260316_143002_3. They also included a brief trace showing long server queue times.
Zach (eng-sre): I'm pulling node metrics for ravenwood-dedicated-1. On it now.
ops-bot: deploy-check: no recent commits to serving in the last 24h.
Zach (eng-sre): Seen it — host redw-ded-7 shows CPU steal spikes coincident with the request times (14:12, 14:32, 14:58 UTC). Kernel steal% jumps to 38-45% then drops. Network and disk look fine.
Ingrid (eng-runtime): If steal% is high, processes are scheduled out — that explains queueing. Which workloads are colocated on that host?
Zach (eng-sre): Looks like a transient spot reclaim/reschedule of a batch training task from partner pool that landed on same hypervisor for ~6-8m. The k8s scheduler allowed binpacking due to low allocatable CPU.
Maria (support): Ravenwood is asking for a fast mitigation — they want either a throttle/allowlist for that tenant or to be bumped to an isolated reserved shard. What's quickest?
Ingrid (eng-runtime): Quick immediate mitigation: move Ravenwood's allocation to the "priority-lane" nodepool (isolated) — that requires a small maintenance window to reschedule pods, but can be done in <10m. Alternative: apply per-tenant soft throttle so long-running embed jobs get rate-limited — lower churn but higher latency for bulk jobs.
Zach (eng-sre): I can migrate them to priority-lane now. Running drain on affected nodes and cordon/taint to avoid future binpacking. Command I ran:
```
kubectl cordon redw-ded-7
kubectl drain redw-ded-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl label node redw-ded-7 evacuated=true
```
Ingrid (eng-runtime): Also updated the autoscaler policy to prefer spreading large CPU requests away from dedicated pools during spot activity window.
Lee (customer-success): I told Ravenwood we'll perform a live migration to an isolated pool, ETA ~8m. Asked them to watch p99 and confirm.
Maria (support): Ravenwood confirmed — seeing immediate improvement on the first sample request (r_20260316_141207_1) p99 down to ~330ms. :white_check_mark:
Zach (eng-sre): Post-migration graphs: p99 returned to baseline across the shard. I'll keep the node cordoned and file a follow-up to trace why the batch landed there.
Ingrid (eng-runtime): Filing infra action item: ensure scheduler's anti-affinity for dedicated pools respects spot/priority hints. Ticket: INFRA-4821.
Lee (customer-success): Closing loop with customer: offered two follow-ups — (1) move Ravenwood permanently to reserved pool (billing impact), (2) add tenant-specific allowlist so they get priority lanes during critical windows. Customer asked for docs on cost delta.
Maria (support): Created support ticket SUP-8920 summarizing incident, root cause (noisy/colocated batch causing CPU steal), immediate mitigation (migration to priority-lane), and P1 follow-ups (scheduler rule + reservation option).
Zach (eng-sre): Noted: add alerting for host CPU steal% > 30% that triggers automated tenant reshuffle for dedicated pools — reduces manual triage time.
Lee (customer-success): Thx team. Marking this resolved for now. Will reopen if Ravenwood reports recurrence.
Ingrid (eng-runtime): TL;DR: p99 spike caused by host-level CPU steal from colocated batch; mitigated by moving tenant to isolated nodepool and cordoning noisy node. Follow-ups: INFRA-4821, SUP-8920, consider automated steal% -> reshape flow.
